touches.text: Sleep is an entry on Cairn's scheduled list (5.9). Since there is one Cairn in the swarm (5.5.3.8.1), Cairn always starts the sleep token, however many boxes there are. At its time Cairn runs its own sleep routine, then hands the sleep token over the bus to the next device, and so on round the rack in the rack's order (5.7.3.3).

What each device does in its sleep depends on the device: the librarian consolidates memory; the learning blocks do the same on their smaller memory sets; Recovery might run backups or SSD checks; some (eg the embeddings device) do nothing.
Cairn's own sleep has a lot to do, including clearing the logging tree of things older than 30 days (4.3.2).
Sleep's base trigger is the clock (2300). Once we can tell how recently things were interacted with, that overrides the clock.

When this box may be used is decided from three inputs: the schedule sets a baseline; observing Akien (how recently things were interacted with) can open time that would otherwise not exist, because measuring trumps rules; and an away window ("going to bed", "out to the theater", x to y) does the same.
It writes one JSON record at the end of a pass listing each device: beat time, device folder found or NOT FOUND, file mtime, pid spawned. It does no checks and no takeover.

The sleep token goes round in sequence, one sleeper at a time, so no one sleeper takes the whole system to everyone else's cost. The order itself doesn't matter: alphabetical by device, then by instance, the same on every box and nothing stored.
The pulse triggers the check: each pulse, the shim checks its device's list against the clock. No match, the pulse is dropped; a match is a PROBE that kicks off that thing in the device (5.6.4.6).
Sleep is one entry on Cairn's list (5.3.3.1).

Cairn owns all of ~/.cairn/ and delegates each ~/.cairn/devices/ subtree to its device. Everything outside devices/ (~/.cairn/logging/ and the rest) is Cairn's, so every log is Cairn's and Cairn cleans them up in sleep. Transient things are files there; trouble tickets are logging items.

Transient things may help debugging out to 30 days and won't be needed past that, eg an inference ticket looked at a week later because a bug turned up. No trouble should stand unresolved at 30 days; sleep's cleanup may be made to spare one that does.
